story.title: Story Behind the Song
story.body: “Nightlight” was written on a sleepless train ride home. It is about holding on to the warmth of someone who is no longer there, those small reminders that still guide you in the dark.

lines.text: The city hums while I’m wide awake
You left a note, the kind that stays
I fold it small, then forget to place
Maybe time will sand the edges down
But some shapes never leave the ground
You’re my nightlight, you don’t fade
When the room goes quiet and the thoughts get loud
You’re the soft glow I can’t replace
Even when I know I should
I water ghosts, they grow on cue
Petals made of all the things we didn’t do
I talk to walls, they talk back too
Say it’s normal, I don’t think it’s true

neon-pillowcase.body: The outside world is leaking into the most private space in the song. It sets up the sleepless feeling before the loss is named directly.

note-that-stays.lyric: You left a note, the kind that stays
note-that-stays.body: This line reflects on the lasting impact of someone’s parting words. Even though the person is gone, the note and what it represents linger. It is a reminder of comfort, love, and unfinished conversations.

sand-the-edges.lyric: Maybe time will sand the edges down
sand-the-edges.body: The narrator wants time to soften the pain, but the image is careful rather than dramatic. Healing here is slow abrasion, not a clean break.

some-shapes.lyric:
Maybe time will sand the edges down
But some shapes never leave the ground
some-shapes.body: These two lines work together: time can make something easier to hold, but it does not always make it disappear. The memory remains part of the room.

nightlight-refrain.lyric: You’re my nightlight, you don’t fade
nightlight-refrain.body: The title image turns grief into something small and useful. It is not a blazing rescue, just enough light to keep moving.

quiet-loud.lyric: When the room goes quiet and the thoughts get loud
quiet-loud.body: This line names the way silence can amplify memory. The contrast makes the chorus feel intimate instead of cinematic.

water-ghosts.lyric: I water ghosts, they grow on cue
water-ghosts.body: The narrator is participating in the haunting by revisiting it. The line suggests that attention can accidentally keep an old feeling alive.

petals.lyric:
I water ghosts, they grow on cue
Petals made of all the things we didn’t do
petals.body: The image stretches across both lines: regret becomes something delicate and blooming, not just heavy. It makes the unfinished future feel strangely alive.
